ἀργός (A), ή, όν,
A.shining, glistening, of a goose, Od. 15.161 ; of a sleek, well-fed ox, Il. 23.30 ; in Hom. mostly in the phrase πόδας ἀργοί, of hounds, swift-footed, because all swift motion causes a kind of glancing or flickering light, 18.578 , Od. 2.11 , etc.; “κύνες ἀργοί”
Il. 1.50
, 18.283 , cf. D.S. 4.41 , Corn. ND 16 .
2. white,
Arist. Top. 149a7 .
II. parox. as pr. n., Ἄργος, ὁ, name of a dog, Swift-foot,
Od. 17.292 : also of the herdsman Argus (i.e. bright-eyed,
A. Pr. 567 (lyr.), Supp. 305 ) who was so called from his eyes being ever open and bright. (By dissimilation from Ἀργρός, cf. Skt. ṛjrá-, = ( 1 ) shining, ( 2 ) swift, Vedic pr. n. [Rnull ]ji-śvan-, lit. = possessing κύνες ἀργοί.)
From A Greek-English Lexicon (Henry George Liddell, Robert Scott, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1940)
